findings.current: One had fainted, while the other had cried until tears and snot streamed down his face in front of everyone.
findings.defect: The nearest plural antecedent is the two men speaking, and the masculine pronoun reinforces that reading, but the surrounding ages and marriage-prospect discussion concern the two young women. This misassigns who fainted and cried.
findings.rationale: Naming the intended pair resolves the internal referent contradiction without changing the event.
findings.replacement: Of the two young women, one had fainted, while the other had cried until tears and snot streamed down her face in front of everyone.

findings.current: At the Shanxi Provincial Office, Assistant Military Commissioner Li Feng confronts Eunuch Hong, who has invited the Three Hands of Zhongnan to entertain the prince. Gong Ilhyuk taunts Li Feng over a defeat at Huashan ten years earlier. When Taekyung’s group arrives, the tense gathering includes Li Feng, Hong Jin, and three young martial artists from the Zhongnan Sect. Taekyung identifies himself as Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family, easing the hostility, then recognizes Zhongnan from a novel he once read before stopping himself from revealing too much.
findings.defect: The summary omits the chapter’s opening Jin Family procession and Jin Mukyung’s unresolved warning that someone at the luncheon is as disgusting as a bug. It also calls the Three Hands young martial artists even though the reading copy does not establish that characterization.
findings.rationale: The replacement restores the omitted forward hook without identifying the person Jin Mukyung means, and avoids adding an unsupported age characterization.
findings.replacement: While the Jin Family’s main party travels through Taiyuan, Jin Wikyung worries that Taekyung may cause trouble at Prince Shangshan’s luncheon. Jin Mukyung says there should be no problem unless Taekyung’s stomach cannot handle someone there who is “as disgusting as a bug.” At the Shanxi Provincial Office, Assistant Military Commissioner Li Feng confronts Eunuch Hong, who has invited the Three Hands of Zhongnan to entertain the prince. summary: The reading copies preserve the packet’s action-comedy voice and established terminology overall, but contain two unclear action referents, two localized prose/grammar issues, and one inconsistent System-panel style. The checkpoint summary also drops Jin Mukyung’s closing hook and twice treats all three Zhongnan representatives as unidentified even though Gong Ilhyuk has been named.
